text.p: Australian pace bowler Jason Gillespie wrecked England with his test-best of seven for 37 in the fourth Ashes test at Headingley on Friday.
England's last seven wickets crashed for only 34 and they were all out for 172 a few minutes before lunch on the second day.
Both Gillespie and Glenn McGrath found a degree of help in the pitch on a bright morning, following a rain-hit first day which England finished on 106 for three.
The day even began promisingly for them, night watchman Dean Headley sticking around for 10 overs before getting out to the first ball of Gillespie's devastating spell.
It was a wide one, which Headley, who had made 22, clipped to Steve Waugh in the gully.
That reward for a bowling change was repeated five overs later as Glenn McGrath returned to capture the prized wicket of Michael Atherton.
The England captain hooked straight to Gillespie at long leg and was gone for the painstaking 41 off 51 overs.
Only four balls later Graham Thorpe, on 15, dragged a delivery from Gillespie into his stumps to deepen England's plight.
Gillespie then had John Crawley caught at short leg for two, the ball apparently bouncing up off the toe of Greg Blewett's boot.
Three more wickets followed in Gillespie's next two overs, starting with Robert Croft. He fell for six to a superb catch by Ricky Pointing, leaping at backward square leg.
Local hero Darren Gough and last man Mike Smith, on his debut, were then bowled for ducks by Gillespie to wrap up the innings.
